purpose: S-desc condition of the Phase 2 localization study (and the agent prompt only if S-desc is adopted). Narrowed to the MSTT-199 entities (arXiv:2409.03110). Source document: research/histotype_mri_descriptions.md; citation numbers refer to its section 5.
rules: <= 60 words each; descriptive only; every claim traceable to the cited sources; claims without a retrieved source (angiosarcoma-specific appearance) are omitted.

F.text: Fibrous tumor (desmoid fibromatosis or undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma): a soft-tissue mass roughly isointense to muscle on T1 and of intermediate-to-high, heterogeneous signal on fat-suppressed T2, where dense collagen forms dark bands. Desmoids have infiltrative margins and often a linear tail along a fascial plane; myxoid or necrotic parts of a sarcoma are brighter on T2.

L.text: Lipomatous tumor (well-differentiated or dedifferentiated liposarcoma): a mass made largely of fat, bright on T1 like subcutaneous fat and dark on fat-suppressed T2, with thick or nodular septa and non-fatty nodules. A dedifferentiated tumor adds a non-fatty solid component, intermediate on T1 and bright on T2, which belongs to the same lesion.
L.notes: Dedifferentiated component wording: abstract-level evidence (Murphey 2005, ref 4) plus researcher inference recorded in section 3 item 2.

M.text: Myxoid tumor (intramuscular myxoma or myxofibrosarcoma): a mass darker than muscle on T1 and very bright, close to fluid, on fat-suppressed T2, so it can resemble a cyst. Myxomas are well circumscribed inside a muscle, often with a thin rim of fat or edema around them; myxofibrosarcomas are more heterogeneous, with ill-defined infiltrative margins and a bright tail along fascia.

N.text: Nerve sheath tumor (schwannoma or malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor): a fusiform mass along the course of a major nerve, low-to-intermediate on T1 and bright on T2. Look for the nerve entering or exiting the mass, fat capping its upper and lower poles (split-fat sign), and ring-like fascicles. Malignant tumors have infiltrative margins and surrounding edema.

V.text: Vascular tumor (hemangioma, vascular malformation, or angiosarcoma): a lobulated, septated mass of tangled serpiginous channels, intermediate-to-low on T1 and strikingly bright on fat-suppressed T2. Look for dark round phleboliths, dark flow voids, fluid-fluid levels, and interspersed fat on T1.
V.notes: No retrieved source describes angiosarcoma MRI appearance; the text covers the benign vascular entities only (evidence gap, section 3 item 3).
